Silicon Rules are the limits and expectations for engaging with Silicon Laws and similar such mechanics.
# SI.0 - Server Rules Take Precedent Silicons are bound to the same rules as crew. Not having a Law that prevents an action is not the same as having a Law that allows an action.
Altered or subverted silicons with the appropriate laws can be considered pseudo-antagonists. They must still adhere to fundamental antagonist limits and expectations.
If you feel you have a law that could be interpreted in a way that breaks server rules, you must ask an admin for permission.
# SI.1 - Laws Law-bound entities must obey all laws to the best of their abilities at all times. If there is a conflict, the Law higher on the list takes precedent. In the event of an ambiguous law, Silicons must be consistent in their interpretation throughout the course of a round.
Silicons may not request a law change. Do not seek out being Emagged, this is considered self-antagging. You are allowed to comply with orders that may see your laws being changed, however.
Silicons with no Laws are considered Free Agents.
Crew and Harm are two common and frequently used terms when it comes to silicon rules. At the bare minimum and unless stated otherwise: - Crew refers to anyone with a valid crew icon. - Harm refers to physical damage to an entity.
You may choose to expand the definition, as long as your actions remain within server rules.
# SI.2 - Orders When a silicon interprets orders in good faith, the person that gave the order is responsible for the outcome.
Intentionally misinterpreting orders is allowed, subject to your laws, however in such a scenario the Silicon is responsible for the outcome.
Law-bound entities cannot be ordered to break Server Rules.
